## AC-1: Galaxy Map Displays Star Systems

**Derived from:** UC-1, FR-1

Scenario: Player views the galaxy map
  Given the game is running and the player is at a station or in space
  When the player opens the galaxy map view
  Then the map displays at least 8 named star systems
  And each star system has at least one station

---

## AC-2: Select Destination from Galaxy Map

**Derived from:** UC-1, FR-1

Scenario: Player selects a destination system
  Given the galaxy map is displayed
  When the player selects a star system
  Then that system is set as the navigation destination
  And the player's current location is highlighted on the map

---

## AC-3: Buy Commodity with Sufficient Funds

**Derived from:** UC-2, FR-2, RULE-3

Scenario: Player buys a commodity they can afford
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient credits for the commodity
  And the player has remaining cargo capacity
  When the player selects a commodity and chooses to buy
  Then the commodity is added to the player's cargo
  And the player's credits are reduced by the purchase price
  And the price shown is specific to this system

---

## AC-4: Buy Commodity Rejected When Insufficient Credits

**Derived from:** UC-2, FR-2

Scenario: Player cannot buy a commodity they cannot afford
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player's credits are less than the commodity price
  When the player attempts to buy the commodity
  Then the purchase is rejected
  And the player is informed that they have insufficient credits
  And the player's credits and cargo are unchanged

---

## AC-5: Sell Commodity from Cargo

**Derived from:** UC-2, FR-2

Scenario: Player sells a commodity they hold
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player's cargo contains the selected commodity
  When the player selects a commodity and chooses to sell
  Then the commodity is removed from the player's cargo
  And the player's credits are increased by the sale price

---

## AC-6: Commodity Prices Differ Between Systems

**Derived from:** UC-2, FR-2, RULE-3

Scenario: Trade routes exist due to price variation
  Given there are at least two star systems with stations
  When a player views commodity prices at each system
  Then at least one commodity has a different price between the two systems

```yaml
properties:
  price_variation:
    description: "At least one commodity has different prices across systems, creating profitable trade routes"
    type: existence
    invariant: "exists commodity C, systems A, B such that price(C, A) != price(C, B)"
    derived_from: RULE-3
```

---

## AC-7: Hyperspace Jump Deducts Fuel and Moves Player

**Derived from:** UC-3, FR-3, RULE-2

Scenario: Player jumps with sufficient fuel
  Given the player is in a star system
  And the player has selected a destination system
  And the player has sufficient fuel for the jump
  When the player initiates a hyperspace jump
  Then fuel is deducted from the ship's fuel tank
  And the player arrives in the destination system

```yaml
properties:
  fuel_deduction:
    description: "Fuel decreases by the jump cost after each successful jump"
    type: monotonicity
    invariant: "fuel_after = fuel_before - jump_cost, where jump_cost > 0"
    bounds:
      fuel_after: ">= 0"
      jump_cost: "> 0"
    derived_from: RULE-2
  fuel_non_negative:
    description: "Fuel is never negative after a jump"
    type: positivity
    invariant: "fuel_after >= 0"
    derived_from: RULE-2
```

---

## AC-8: Hyperspace Jump Rejected When Insufficient Fuel

**Derived from:** UC-3, FR-3, RULE-2

Scenario: Player cannot jump without enough fuel
  Given the player is in a star system
  And the player's fuel is less than the jump cost
  When the player attempts a hyperspace jump
  Then the jump is prevented
  And the player is informed of insufficient fuel
  And the player remains in the current system

```yaml
properties:
  fuel_guard:
    description: "A jump with insufficient fuel never succeeds"
    type: bounds
    invariant: "if fuel < jump_cost then jump_succeeds = false"
    derived_from: RULE-2
```

---

## AC-9: Pirate Encounter Triggered on Jump

**Derived from:** UC-4, FR-4

Scenario: Pirate appears after jump
  Given the player completes a hyperspace jump
  When the encounter check results in a pirate encounter
  Then the player transitions from travel to combat state
  And an AI-controlled pirate is presented for combat

---

## AC-10: Combat Resolves When Pirate Destroyed

**Derived from:** UC-5, FR-5

Scenario: Player destroys a pirate
  Given the player is in ship-to-ship combat with a pirate
  When the pirate's hull is reduced to zero
  Then combat ends
  And the combat kill is recorded toward the player's Elite rating

---

## AC-11: Player Destruction Ends Game

**Derived from:** UC-5, FR-5

Scenario: Player's ship is destroyed in combat
  Given the player is in ship-to-ship combat
  When the player's hull is reduced to zero
  Then the game ends

---

## AC-12: Flee from Combat

**Derived from:** UC-6, FR-5

Scenario: Player successfully flees combat
  Given the player is in ship-to-ship combat
  When the player chooses to flee
  Then either the disengage succeeds and the player continues to the destination
  Or the disengage fails and the player remains in combat

---

## AC-13: Purchase Ship Upgrade with Sufficient Credits

**Derived from:** UC-7, FR-6

Scenario: Player buys an upgrade they can afford
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient credits for the upgrade
  When the player selects and purchases a ship upgrade
  Then the upgrade is applied to the player's ship immediately
  And the player's credits are reduced by the upgrade cost

---

## AC-14: Upgrade Rejected When Insufficient Credits

**Derived from:** UC-7, FR-6

Scenario: Player cannot buy an upgrade they cannot afford
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player's credits are less than the upgrade cost
  When the player attempts to purchase the upgrade
  Then the purchase is rejected
  And the player is informed of insufficient credits
  And the ship's stats and credits are unchanged

---

## AC-15: Save Game Persists All State

**Derived from:** UC-8, FR-7

Scenario: Player saves the game
  Given the player is in an active game session
  When the player invokes the save command
  Then the system serializes and stores credits, cargo, ship stats, current position, and Elite rating
  And the system confirms the save was successful

---

## AC-16: Load Game Restores State or Starts Fresh

**Derived from:** UC-9, FR-7, RULE-1

Scenario: Player loads a previously saved game
  Given a saved game exists from a previous session
  When the player invokes the load command
  Then the game restores credits, cargo, ship stats, position, and Elite rating to match the saved data

Scenario: New game starts with default conditions when no save exists
  Given no saved game exists
  When the player starts the game
  Then the player begins docked at a station with 100 credits and a small cargo hold

```yaml
properties:
  starting_conditions:
    description: "A new game always starts with the defined initial values"
    type: identity
    invariant: "new_game.credits = 100 and new_game.cargo_capacity = small and new_game.location = station"
    derived_from: RULE-1
  save_restore_identity:
    description: "Loading a save produces state identical to the saved state"
    type: identity
    invariant: "load(save(state)) == state"
    derived_from: FR-7
```

---

## AC-17: Server Health Endpoint Returns Healthy

**Derived from:** UC-10, FR-8

Scenario: Health check succeeds when server is running
  Given the game server is running
  When a request is sent to the health endpoint
  Then a healthy status response is returned

---

## AC-18: HUD Displays Ship Status

**Derived from:** UC-11, FR-9

Scenario: Player views the HUD during gameplay
  Given the game is running and the player is in a gameplay screen
  When the player views the heads-up display
  Then the HUD displays the current shield level
  And the HUD displays the current fuel level
  And the HUD displays the current cargo contents
  And the HUD displays the current credit balance

---

## AC-19: Elite Rating Progresses with Profit and Kills

**Derived from:** UC-12, FR-10, RULE-4

Scenario: Elite rating advances when thresholds are crossed
  Given the player has completed trades and combat
  When the accumulated profit and combat kills cross a rating tier threshold
  Then the player's Elite rating advances to the next tier
  And the updated rating is displayed

```yaml
properties:
  rating_monotonicity:
    description: "Elite rating never decreases when profit or kills increase"
    type: monotonicity
    invariant: "if accumulated_profit increases or combat_kills increases then rating_tier never decreases"
    derived_from: RULE-4
  rating_non_negative:
    description: "Accumulated stats are never negative"
    type: positivity
    invariant: "accumulated_profit >= 0 and combat_kills >= 0"
    derived_from: RULE-4
  tier_progression:
    description: "Each tier requires equal or greater stats than the previous tier"
    type: monotonicity
    invariant: "threshold(tier_N+1) >= threshold(tier_N) for all tiers"
    derived_from: RULE-4
```

---

## AC-20: Game Renders at 60 FPS

**Derived from:** NFR-1

Scenario: Rendering performance meets target
  Given the game is running in Google Chrome on a 2020 laptop
  When the player engages in standard gameplay (navigation, trading, or combat)
  Then the game renders at no less than 60 frames per second

---

## AC-21: Game Operates Fully Offline

**Derived from:** NFR-2

Scenario: No external network requests during gameplay
  Given the game is started
  When the player plays the game
  Then all assets, scripts, and styles are served locally
  And no requests are made to external CDN hosts

---

## AC-22: Game Starts with One Command

**Derived from:** NFR-3

Scenario: Fresh install and startup
  Given a clean checkout of the game repository
  When the command `npm install && npm start` is executed
  Then the game starts and is playable
  And no manual build steps, configuration, or additional commands are required

---

## AC-23: All User-Facing Text Is in English

**Derived from:** NFR-4

Scenario: User-facing language verification
  Given the game is running
  When the player views any screen (galaxy map, trading, combat, HUD, menus)
  Then all displayed text is in English
